items.title: Fields, complete local rings, the integers, one-dimensional local and Nagata rings, and Dedekind domains of characteristic zero are J-2
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition collects seven classes of rings that are J-2. The proof checks the relevant criterion for each class: for fields, the integers, one-dimensional Nagata rings and Dedekind domains with fraction field of characteristic zero it verifies the condition on finite purely inseparable extensions of residue fields, carrying out the one-dimensional Nagata case in detail, where either the prime is maximal, so the extension is finite over a regular ring, or it is minimal, where the Nagata condition makes the integral closure in the extension finite and hence a one-dimensional normal, therefore regular, domain. For complete local rings and for one-dimensional local rings it uses the criterion on finite extensions instead, reducing the first to the statement that a complete local domain is J-0 and observing in the second case that the regular locus is stable under generalisation on a finite spectrum.
